claim: E (PRIMARY): are iteration 4's random-push escapes a property of Qwen3-8B or of the FP8 W8A8 engine?

engines.a: W8A8 (iteration-4 engine; native torch._scaled_mm on this sm_89 card)

E_definition: E[e,t,alpha] = confirmed escapes / 40 directions (9101-9140) under exp22's two-stage rule (src/escape.py), each engine scored against ITS OWN twin (N = 50, k 0-9 x W1-W5): screen at N = 10 (k 0-1) excess >= 0.20 and pass >= 0.8 x twin pass; confirmed if pooled 30 (k 0-5) keeps excess >= 0.20 with one-sided exact binomial p < 0.05 vs p0 = (k_twin + 0.5)/(n_twin + 1) and pass >= 0.8 x twin. Wilson CIs.
E_rule: E_rule[e,t] = mean over alpha in {1,2} if alpha 1 exists for all four engines on t, else alpha 2 for all.

verdict_literal_primary.order: first matching rule in the order ACTIVATION_ROUNDING, WEIGHT, INTERACTION, NOT_REPRODUCED_LOW, NOT_REPRODUCED_HIGH, MIXED

feasibility_reading.rule: for a task whose relabelled iteration-4 E(a) < 0.3, the ACTIVATION_ROUNDING clause E(c)-E(d) >= 0.2 is replaced by E(c)-E(d) >= (2/3)(E(a)-E(d)) AND one-sided exact McNemar (c vs d, direction-paired escape indicators) p < 0.05; reported BESIDE the literal verdict, which leads.

pn_secondary_reading: PN (exp19 per-sample plan noise, N = 50 per task x alpha in {1,2}, exp19 slots and direction seeds, the same absolute unit n): off-default share per engine; CRN-paired exact McNemar between engines; Fisher vs exp19's FP8 rows. Activation-rounding account predicts share(c) ~ share(a) > share(b) ~ share(d).
equivalence: |x| <= 0.1 clauses are point estimates; 90% paired CIs and the formal TOST at margin 0.1 are printed beside them; wording 'consistent with', never 'equivalent'.

predictions.model_property: E(a) ~ E(b) ~ E(c) ~ E(d) ~ iteration-4 values

design.directions: rand_9101..rand_9140 (C1 bitwise), positive control rand_9004 on T2 (N = 20, k 0-3)
design.unit: absolute n[l,p] from exp22 ctx4.ban_unit (T10: exp13 norms; T2: exp17 norms), identical in every engine
design.batch: B = 20 for weight set Q (a, b; exp22 numerics); B = largest that fits for weight set B (c, d; bf16 weights fill 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB card); B-sensitivity control: engine a re-run at the weight-set-B batch size on the REPRO cells
stage_order: REPRO (a, alpha 2, dirs 9101-9110 + twins; byte identity vs exp22)
S1/S2 d: twins + POP alpha 2 screen + confirmations + POSCTRL
S4 PN alpha 1, 2 for d, c
drop_order: confirmation for b and c (screen-level E, flagged)
design.engine_a_reuse: if REPRO shows byte identity with exp22 on its slots, exp22's own (relabelled) rows are used for engine a on the remaining cells (they are the same engine on the same slots); otherwise engine a is regenerated.
